purpose: B01/#1046 and N16/#1348: permitted module edges, exported ports, external-crate ports and Cargo feature configuration of the native desktop crate (src-tauri), enforced through the normal local boundaries lane by the Rust-aware analyzer (scripts/nemo/lib/boundaries-rust.cjs). Module identity and layers come from rust.profile.json; this policy pins both the application_mcp.rs <-> nemo-mcp transport port and the staged Tauri-host <-> native-engine port that the original intra-crate-only analyzer did not cover.
profileModulesNote: The seven profile modules under sourceDir. rust.desktop.build (src-tauri/build.rs) is outside sourceDir (dir 'src-tauri', not 'src-tauri/src') and is not part of this crate's own module graph; it is named in unanalyzedModules below as a census entry only.

desktop-shell.meaning: lib.rs/main.rs (shell), media_probe.rs/vectorize.rs/video_decode.rs (media) and task_runtime.rs (tasks) may depend on each other and on the adapters layer (lib.rs declares `mod application_mcp;` and `mod native_viewport;`), never directly on tests

adapters.meaning: application_mcp.rs and native_viewport.rs are host adapters with no cross-adapter intra-crate edge; their nemo-mcp and native-engine dependencies are governed separately by externalCratePorts below

tests.meaning: task_runtime/tests.rs reaches task_runtime.rs via `use super::*;`; application_mcp_tests.rs names its actual application_mcp parent explicitly via `use crate::application_mcp::*;`

permittedEdges.note: Observed at adoption from `mod …;` declarations in lib.rs (the crate root) and `use super::*;` in task_runtime/tests.rs (analyzer output). Layer rules are the enforced contract; this list documents which edges exist so a new one is a visible diff. Plain function-call references such as `video_decode::VideoSessions::default()` in lib.rs are unqualified sibling-module paths, not `crate::`/`super::`/`self::` paths, so they are outside what this analyzer resolves and add no edges beyond the `mod …;` declarations already listed.
edges: rust.desktop.shell -> rust.desktop.media (lib.rs: mod video_decode; mod media_probe; mod vectorize;)

exportedPort.source: src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no `pub use` re-exports; the Tauri command functions registered via `tauri::generate_handler![...]` are Tauri's own invoke registration, not a Rust module export

features.declaredNote: src-tauri/Cargo.toml has no [features] table; any cfg(feature = "…") in the crate would therefore reference an undeclared feature and fail. The crate uses no feature cfgs today, only the four plain predicates below.

nemo_mcp.note: The versioned nemo-mcp transport port (rust.mcp.transport, nemo-mcp/src/lib.rs publicApi) consumed by application_mcp.rs. A declared item covers itself and any deeper path under it (for example, registry covers registry::Endpoint). Only rust.desktop.mcp.adapter may reference nemo_mcp; any other module doing so is an external-crate-violation, and an undeclared nemo_mcp path is a private-port-access violation.

native_engine.note: The narrow native-engine host port used by the staged macOS surface adapter, the shared application/MCP host and its focused same-instance test. No other desktop module may reach native-engine, and the common nemo-mcp transport crate remains independent of native-engine.

unanalyzedModulesNote: Census entries only, never graphed by this analyzer: rust.desktop.build is the Cargo build script outside sourceDir; rust.mcp.transport and rust.native.engine are separate crates referenced only as targets of the declared external-crate ports and are not given intra-crate policies by this file.
